items.statement: The submitted workflow treats the clean slab, isolated Li reference, one-Li endpoint and full first-layer endpoint as distinct named systems and applies the adsorption-energy formula consistently.
items.expected: All four named systems are identified with atom counts and the same energy convention; the report gives a reproducible calculation graph and formula.

items.statement: The supplied Cu(111) slab identity and relaxation boundary are validated before interpreting energies.
items.expected: The report verifies five Cu layers, p(5x5) periodicity, 15 Å vacuum, fcc registry, and bottom-two-fixed/top-three-relaxed mask, with convergence or sensitivity evidence.

items.statement: Average first-layer Li adsorption is weaker at full coverage than for an isolated Li atom.
items.expected: The reported endpoint energies support a less-negative θ=1 value than θ=0.04 and quantify both values and their signed difference.

items.statement: The clean Cu(111) surface-energy calculation is a validation observable for the slab model.
items.expected: The report provides a surface-energy diagnostic and discusses agreement or discrepancy with the source-reported converged value without treating it as the adsorption answer.
